name: Question 9
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Q$ shown above. Find the matrix $R$ such that $A=QR$ is a QR factorization of $A.$
worked_solution:
Since $Q$ has orthonormal columns, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}^{T}\cdot A & ={Q}^{T}\cdot QR \\ {Q}^{T}\,A & =({Q}^{T}\,Q)R \\ {Q}^{T}\,A & ={I}_{2}R \\ R & ={Q}^{T}\,A\end{aligned}
$$

 

Note that ${Q}^{T}Q={I}_{2}$ since the columns of $Q$ are orthonormal.

Now, we calculate the matrix $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3} & -\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} \\ 0 & \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

A=[2−12−2−21],Q=[131613−26−13−16] Consider the matrices A and Q shown above. Find the matrix R such that A=QR is a QR factorization of A.

a
R=[23−43026]
b
R=[3−330−16]
c
R=[3233016]
d
R=[23−233026]
e
R=[232330−16]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since Q has orthonormal columns, pre-multiplying both sides of A=QR by QT, we obtain

QT⋅A=QT⋅QRQTA=(QTQ)RQTA=I2RR=QTA

Note that QTQ=I2 since the columns of Q are orthonormal.

Now, we calculate the matrix R:

R=QTA=[1313−1316−26−16][2−12−2−21]=[23−43026].
